About me

Good models start with understanding the data, not just fitting it.

I'm Ashraf Hebish, an AI & Data Science student at Horus University, Egypt. I work across two connected fields: Data Analysis & Statistics and Machine Learning.

On the data side, I clean datasets and analyse them with descriptive statistics, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests and ANOVA, often implementing the formulas myself in Python before relying on libraries.

On the machine learning side, I train linear regression models and evaluate them with R², RMSE and MAE, and I'm studying AI at university and through a diploma at Arabian Academy.

I turn this work into simple web apps that open from a single link, and I enjoy hardware too, like a security system I built entirely from logic gates.

02 02 / Machine Learning · House Prices

Smart Regression System

Train simple or multiple linear regression on a 200-house sample or your own CSV, then read the model through charts, metrics and plain recommendations.

  • Actual vs predicted chart, residual plots and a correlation matrix

03 03 / Horus University · Faculty of AI

Numerical Methods Lab

Presented · Best Numerical Methods Calculator competition, Faculty of AI · May 2026

An interactive lab that solves equations and linear systems with six numerical methods and draws every iteration on a live chart. Built as a team project of 10–12 students; I presented it at the faculty competition.

  • Bisection · False Position · Newton-Raphson · Secant · Thomas · Jacobi
  • Step-by-step mode and a log-scale convergence chart
  • Method comparison, history and JSON export
  • JavaScript
  • Chart.js
  • Numerical Analysis
Live demo ↗
04 04 / The Healthcare Project

Statistical Analysis Pipeline

Upload any CSV file. The app detects numeric and categorical columns, then runs a 12-phase analysis from cleaning to conclusions.

  • Formulas written by hand with Python's math module, without SciPy
  • Confidence intervals, t-test and ANOVA
  • Built-in sample dataset
  • Python
  • JavaScript
  • Statistics
  • CSV
Live demo ↗ Code
05 05 / Logic Design · Hardware

Digital Logic Security System

An access-control system built only from logic gates and basic components. It compares the code a user enters with a stored key code and shows the result with LEDs.

  • 4-bit key code and data entry switches compared with XOR gates
  • Green LED for a correct code, red LED for a wrong one, with an Enter control
  • I designed the circuit, built and tested it on a breadboard, and made the wooden enclosure
  • Digital Logic
  • XOR / NOR Gates
  • Breadboard
  • Hardware Prototype
